messages:
maya: FYI I opened a PR that narrows the Vault/KMS surface for the onprem auth proxy. touches: config/auth/* and infra/vpc/egress. link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/pull/482
liam: on it. is this purely config or do we have code paths that will require a migration?
maya: primarily config + a small flag in auth-proxy that flips behavior. no DB migrations. code change is 6 lines: `if (KV_SCOPE === 'minimal') { denyExternalEgress() }`
ryan: sec-bot will run checks but quick q: does this affect service-to-service keys or just user creds?
maya: S2S keys unchanged. this restricts token minting scopes and the default egress rules for onprem clusters.
sec-bot: Automated scan: secrets-check: PASS (no new plaintext), kms-policy-lint: WARN - policy 3 allows broad read in staging. See details: https://security.redwood.ai/scans/482
olivia: @maya can you tighten policy 3 before merge? small tweak: replace `read:*` with `read:tokens` where possible.
maya: yeah will do. quick question for merge timing — we want to land before next dedicated deploy (Thu 10:00 UTC). any objections?
liam: oncall alignment: if we merge before Thu 02:00 UTC we can run a staged rollout and watch for egress logs. otherwise push to next window.
ryan: also please add a short note in the PR description about rollback steps and the flag to revert, e.g. `KV_SCOPE=legacy`
maya: added rollback section and updated policy as @olivia suggested. pushed new commit.
olivia: reading now... looks good. :thumbsup: one tiny nit about comment wording but not blocking.
sec-bot: Re-scan: secrets-check: PASS, kms-policy-lint: PASS
liam: approved from infra side. @olivia or @ryan can we get final security ack to avoid blocking the Thu slot?
olivia: ack from security. LGTM.
ryan: ack from platform. go ahead and queue for merge in the Thu 02:00 UTC window.
maya: thanks all — I'll queue the merge and ping oncall when deploy starts. :rocket:
__notes: This thread is a short coordination thread for a PR with security implications (secrets, KMS, VPC egress) and includes an automated bot scan. Messages are concise to reflect Slack style.
